topics.name: AI Automation for Solopreneurs
details: **What is happening:** AI-powered tools are rapidly becoming indispensable for solopreneurs, automating tasks like customer service, email marketing, content creation, and administrative functions. Agentic AI, capable of autonomous workflows, is emerging as a significant trend for 2026.

**Why it matters:** FieldWork content can focus on practical AI implementation guides, tool reviews, and strategies for leveraging AI to reclaim time, boost productivity, and scale a one-person business without increasing workload.

topics.name: The 4-Day Work Week Movement
details: **What is happening:** The 4-day work week is gaining significant momentum globally, with pilot programs demonstrating improved employee well-being, reduced burnout, increased productivity, and even higher revenue for businesses. Many companies are making the switch permanent.

**Why it matters:** FieldWork can address how solopreneurs can strategically implement a 4-day work week, optimize their business model for fewer working hours, and achieve work-life balance while maintaining or increasing income.

topics.name: Digital Detox & Offline Living
details: **What is happening:** Driven by digital fatigue and a desire to escape constant connectivity, entrepreneurs are increasingly seeking digital detox strategies and embracing analog activities. This trend is seen as essential for psychological well-being, enhancing focus, creativity, and decision-making.

**Why it matters:** FieldWork content can explore strategies for intentional disconnection, building offline habits, and integrating more nature and human connection into life, aligning with the "Live Offline" aspect of the program.

topics.name: Anti-Hustle & Slow Entrepreneurship
details: **What is happening:** There's a rising movement among entrepreneurs rejecting the "growth at all costs" mentality in favor of sustainable, purpose-driven businesses that prioritize well-being, quality, and depth of relationships over rapid expansion.

**Why it matters:** FieldWork can resonate with this audience by offering content on building a business that aligns with personal values, achieving financial freedom without burnout, and defining success on one's own terms.

topics.name: Reclaiming Time through Strategic Delegation
details: **What is happening:** Many founders and solopreneurs struggle with spending excessive time on low-value, administrative tasks, which hinders business growth. There's a strong emphasis on identifying these tasks and strategically delegating or outsourcing them.

**Why it matters:** FieldWork can provide actionable frameworks, tools, and mindset shifts for founders to effectively delegate, outsource, and automate non-core activities, freeing up time for high-impact strategic work.

topics.name: Working Less, Earning More Strategies
details: **What is happening:** Entrepreneurs are actively seeking proven methods to maximize income while minimizing working hours. This involves mastering time management, focusing on high-impact activities, and leveraging technology and smart systems.

**Why it matters:** FieldWork can offer advanced productivity techniques, business model optimization strategies, and insights into creating leverage to achieve financial abundance without sacrificing personal time.

topics.name: Entrepreneurial Well-being & Burnout Prevention
details: **What is happening:** There's a growing recognition of the direct link between an entrepreneur's well-being and their business performance. Strategies for preventing burnout, managing stress, and fostering mental health are becoming critical topics.

**Why it matters:** FieldWork can integrate well-being practices, stress management techniques, and strategies for maintaining a healthy work-life balance into its curriculum, positioning itself as a holistic program for sustainable entrepreneurship.

topics.name: Time & Location Freedom (Modern Nomadism)
details: **What is happening:** The desire for time and location independence continues to be a strong motivator for solopreneurs, evolving beyond traditional digital nomadism to encompass flexible work arrangements that allow for greater personal autonomy and travel.

**Why it matters:** FieldWork can highlight how its program enables founders to build businesses that provide the flexibility to work from anywhere, travel, and spend more time on personal pursuits, embodying the "Build Online. Live Offline." ethos.

hooks: I'm okay with a business that doesn't grow 100% every year, and I think that confuses a lot of people.
I'm okay with not being 'always on' for my business, and I think that makes some gurus uncomfortable.
I'm okay with building a business that lets me be offline more, and I think that breaks the internet's rules.
I'm okay with my business serving my life, not the other way around, and I think that's a radical idea to some.

talking_points: I'm okay with my business serving my life, not the other way around, and I think that's a pretty radical idea to some people.
The standard advice you hear online is to sacrifice everything for your business. Your time, your relationships, your health. You are told to scale at all costs.
But I have seen where that path leads. It leads to burnout. It leads to founders who build a beautiful prison for themselves, chained to a desk and missing the life they were trying to create.
My entire philosophy is built on the opposite idea. We build online so we can live offline.
The business should be a tool. It's an engine that you design for one specific purpose: to buy back your time and your freedom.
This is about setting up smart systems and automation that work for you, so you are not the bottleneck in your own business.
It means you can actually take that afternoon to go for a hike, or be fully present with your family, without worrying that everything will fall apart.
It is not about building a billion dollar company. It is about building a business that funds a rich, fulfilling life out in the world.
If you're a founder or an expert who wants to build a business that gives you more life, not less, then FieldWork is for you. You can learn more at the link in my bio.

talking_points: Share this with a founder who feels trapped by the business they built.
You can and you will find your way back. You have everything you need right now to build a business that gives you your life back, instead of taking it.
I'm recording this because I know this feeling. It's that quiet dread on a beautiful afternoon when you know you 'should' be working.
It's a painful trade off. You feel guilty for working, and you feel guilty for not working.
I get messages every day from founders who are hitting their revenue goals but losing themselves. They're succeeding by every metric except the one that matters: their own freedom.
The hustle culture will tell you this is the price of success. It is not.
You have to keep your eyes on the real reason you started. Your relationships, your health, your time spent in the real world. That is the actual scoreboard.
Your kids, your partner, and your friends won't remember your quarterly earnings reports. They will only remember if you were present.
This is me, right now, choosing to connect with you instead of optimizing a funnel. I'm showing you that it's possible to build a business that doesn't demand every waking second.
You can build a business that runs itself, so you can return to the field. If you want to see how we do it, check out FieldWork.
ideas.body_copy: Share this with a founder who feels trapped by the very thing they built. You can and you will find your way back. You have everything inside you right now to build a business that gives you your life back, instead of taking it. I know that feeling. It's the quiet dread on a beautiful afternoon when your phone buzzes and pulls you away from the present moment. It's a painful trade. You feel guilty for working and guilty for not working. I get messages every day from founders succeeding by every metric except the one that actually matters: their own time and freedom. The hustle culture tells you this is just the price of admission. It is not. Your kids won't remember your revenue charts. Your friends won't remember how many hours you worked. They will only remember if you showed up. This is proof you can choose to be present. You can build the engines for your business and then return to your life. That is what 'Build Online, Live Offline' is all about.
script: Hook: Address the founder trapped by their own success.

Reframe the true legacy: being present for loved ones.

guidance: Film as a simple, grounded talking head video. A warm, natural setting like a porch or near a window is better than a sterile office.
Use B-roll that contrasts the two worlds: a shot of a packed digital calendar, then a shot of an empty field. A shot of someone on a Zoom call, then a shot of someone hiking.
On-screen text should be minimal. Use key phrases like 'They remember if you were present' and 'Build Online. Live Offline.'
The tone should be calm and reassuring, not desperate. Like a friend sharing honest advice around a campfire.
